name: Bothell
seo_title: 5 Christmas Events for Kids in Bothell, WA 2026
seo_desc: 5 Christmas events for kids in Bothell, WA, 3 free: Lights at the Landing at the Park at Bothell Landing and more.
lede: Bothell celebrates Christmas on historic Main Street, where Santa arrives on a fire truck to light a tree named Lucky, and in free light displays from downtown to the north end of town.
celebrates: The Bothell Tree Lighting Festival is the big night downtown: a holiday market on Main Street, free goodies and activities from local merchants, and Santa riding in on a Bothell Fire Department truck to light Lucky, the Main Street tree, before selfies at a local shop. The City of Bothell sets up Lights at the Landing, a free walk through light display in the Park at Bothell Landing. In north Bothell, Evergreen Church runs Evergreen Christmas Lights with a light show set to music, light tunnels and a model train. McMenamins Anderson School adds Breakfast with Santa.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Bothell ran Lights at the Landing from December 1, 2025, into early January at the Park at Bothell Landing, 9919 NE 180th Street. The city listed it as a free holiday light installation on display all day, with parking at the park, and invited families to bundle up, grab a favorite warm drink and wander through the twinkling lights with friends and furry companions.
facts: Bothell is named for David Bothell, a Pennsylvanian who bought land here in 1885 and opened the Bothell Hotel. When neighbors chose a post office name, Gerhard Ericksen said there were so many Bothells in town that it was a good name. Bothell incorporated on April 14, 1909, with David's son George as first mayor. In 1913 a mayor was arrested for going faster than the 12 mile per hour limit on the river bridge; the case was dismissed.
trains: The railroad shaped early Bothell. In 1888 the Seattle, Lake Shore and Eastern Railroad built its line through town toward the Issaquah coal mines, and in 1890 the depot, at first a boxcar, was loaded onto a flatcar and moved to the south bank of the river. Passenger trains ended in 1938 and the line was abandoned in 1971 to become the Burke Gilman Trail. Kids can still see a G gauge model train at Evergreen Christmas Lights, and the Northwest Railway Museum is a drive east.

Bothell's Main Street tree has its own name, Lucky, and Santa lights it each year.

kidfact: Bothell's Christmas tree has a name. It is called Lucky, and every year Santa himself rides in on a fire truck to light it.
faq: When is the Bothell tree lighting?

The Bothell Tree Lighting Festival takes place on a Saturday in early December on Main Street at 102nd Avenue NE. A holiday market runs in the afternoon, local merchants offer free goodies and kids' activities, and Santa arrives on a Bothell Fire Department fire truck to light Lucky, the Main Street tree, followed by selfies with Santa.
Are there free Christmas lights in Bothell?

Yes. The City of Bothell's Lights at the Landing is a free walk through display at the Park at Bothell Landing, 9919 NE 180th Street, with parking at the park. In north Bothell, Evergreen Christmas Lights at Evergreen Church is also free, with free cookies, free parking, light tunnels and a model train display.
Where can kids have breakfast with Santa in Bothell?

McMenamins Anderson School, 18607 Bothell Way NE, holds Breakfast with Santa in Haynes' Hall each December. Tickets are sold by the table of eight and include breakfast and non-alcoholic drinks such as hot chocolate and juice. McMenamins welcomes all ages and suggests bringing a camera for photos with Santa.
How did Bothell get its name?

Bothell is named for David Bothell, who bought 80 acres here in 1885 and built the Bothell Hotel. When residents chose a post office name, store owner Gerhard Ericksen said there were so many Bothells in town that it was a good name. The town incorporated in 1909 with George Bothell as mayor.
Did trains ever run through Bothell?

Yes. The Seattle, Lake Shore and Eastern Railroad built through Bothell in 1888, and the first depot was a boxcar. Passenger service ended in 1938, and after the line was abandoned in 1971 it became the Burke Gilman Trail, the popular walking and biking path that still runs past downtown Bothell today.
